For the accuracy class circled numerals, I can transcribe as (I) and (II) with circled representation. Since the markings are drawn circles around I and II, I could use Ⓘ and Ⓙ? Actually circled Roman numerals: Ⅰ is U+2160. Circled: there's no standard circled Roman numeral in Unicode widely supported... There's Ⓘ? No, Ⓘ is circled capital I (letter I). Ⓙ is circled J. Hmm, that's not Roman numeral II. Better to just use "(Ⅰ)" or "(I)" with a note? The instruction says do not annotate. I'll transcribe as (I) and (II) — perhaps using Ⅰ and Ⅱ characters. The circles are drawn around them. I'll write them as (I) and (II) — but maybe use the circled letters Ⓘ and Ⓙ? That would be wrong. I'll use (Ⅰ) and (Ⅱ) — Roman numeral characters inside parentheses, which approximates the circled marks. Actually, to convey the circle, I could write "( Ⅰ )" with spaces. Hmm. Simplest: transcribe as "I" and "II" in circles notation like (I) and (II). The reading order: "for accuracy classes (I), (II)". That seems fine.

For the logo (eagle/Bundesadler), I should transcribe embedded text in images — the logo has no text. I could note it as an image description... The rules say text embedded in images (logos...) must be transcribed too. The logo doesn't contain readable text. I might include an alt-text style description like "[Bundesadler emblem]" — but "do not annotate". Hmm. Maybe use markdown image syntax with alt text: ![Bundesadler emblem](logo). That's a transcription approach. I'll include something minimal like *[Federal eagle emblem]* — that's annotation-ish but it's transcribing the image content. I think using an image reference with alt text is the cleanest way.
